angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 406,985 km at 154.13 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.4879 +/- 0.0158 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 154.13 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.585 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Dransfield et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4666 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag448D/abstract): 406,985 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.576 +/- 0.012 solar masses from Dransfield et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4666 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag448D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3793 +/- 80 K from Dransfield et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4666 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag448D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dransfield et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4666 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag448D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4666.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.664, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4666 (pscomppars): spectral type M2±0.5, from Dransfield et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag448D/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4666 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.79 dex, from Dransfield et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag448D/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4666 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.19518, from Dransfield et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag448D/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4666 (pscomppars): age 3 Gyr, from Dransfield et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547ag448D/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4666 (pscomppars): rotation period 15.3 d, from Frensch et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A..73F/abstract)
